newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says Nigeria exports not hit by output loss.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Nigeria exports not hit by output loss.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch/Shell is losing 100,000 barrels of crude oil daily after shutting six flow stations due to a feud between two villages, a senior company official said on Monday.
But he said sabotage was not the cause and the production loss was not affecting crude exports.

"We shut down operations on Saturday at the flow stations in the Western Division. Over 100 Shell staff and contractors are trapped in the area but from latest reports they are safe," the official told Reuters in Lagos.
According to the official, the Western Division produces an average 450,000 bpd. Shell produces almost half of Nigeria's two million bpd of crude.
The Shell official said the transfer of a municipal council headquarters was responsible for the dispute between the Ogidigben and Ogbe-Ijoh villages in midwestern Warri town.
The council headquarters was relocated by the military government from Ogidigben to Ogbe-Ijoh before the municipal elections on March 15, a move that irked the villagers, he said.

"Heads of both villages did not demand anything from us but said we won't operate there until the matter is resolved," he said, adding that the company wants to resume operations and was already engaged in dialogue with the villages.
Such feuds are common among villages in Nigeria.
